scenarios.name: launch_burnout_landing_still
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: a sustained 8 g launch, the burnout timeout, a laser landing past one spike, then still. The first tick records setting as external: plan B starts with no stage seen.

scenarios.name: stale_agl_at_apogee
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: the flight lost at apogee -- a stale laser extrapolating -9.6 m must not land the glider at 274 m; the baro fallback lands it once the elevation really comes down.

scenarios.name: stale_barometer_never_launches
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: a stale baro extrapolating past launch_alt_m is no launch; one fresh 15 m sample is no launch either; 15 m held launch_ms is.

divergence.note: the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad

scenarios.name: transient_and_leaky_launch
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: a transient high g is no launch; then the leaky dwell -- dips drain the credit instead of wiping it, so a boost with dropouts still launches on 100 ms of NET time.

scenarios.name: barometer_launch_backup_then_apogee
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: a marginal 2 g boost is caught by the baro backup (held launch_ms), then the apogee: the arming window blinds a burn spike, the IIR smoother is seeded by the first armed reading, one sample below the peak is inside the drop band, a ramp opens the dwell and launch_ms later it deploys.

divergence.note: the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad
plan B's BOOSTING reaches the port as a move from outside, recorded external; every later step is plan B's

scenarios.name: operator_hold
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: a held stage ignores a sustained launch; `stage setting` is a return to the ground, not a hold, and the launch is detected afresh; `stage auto` releases a hold in place.

scenarios.name: missing_readings_never_advance
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: no reading on any channel -- no launch, no crash, however long; a held flight with no readings stays in GLIDING until the RSO backstop.

scenarios.name: apogee_arming_window
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: entering BOOSTING (a warm start here) starts the arming clock; a burn spike then a 60 m "drop" inside the window neither deploys nor seeds the peak; the burnout timeout runs regardless.

scenarios.name: flight_timeout_backstop
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: the separation switch moves BOOSTING to GLIDING (recorded as external), every landing sensor is silent, and flight_timeout_ms after BOOSTING entry the RSO backstop forces DONE.

scenarios.name: external_moves_are_recorded_once
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: a move from outside the sequencer is recorded as external once; the sequencer's own advance is recorded with its reason and never again as external; a separation outside BOOSTING moves nothing.

scenarios.name: landing_timeout
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: warm into LANDING, carried at 1.6 g (never still) -- the landing timeout fires at land_timeout_ms after the entry tick, and not a tick early.

scenarios.name: setting_forgets_the_last_flight
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: warm into GLIDING bases the RSO backstop there; `stage setting` puts the board back on the pad and forgets it, so the backstop never fires from SETTING.

scenarios.name: gnss_elevation_on_the_pad
scenarios.note: test_sequencer: the baros stale, the GNSS elevation (zeroed at its first fix, metres of noise) reads 15 m held well past launch_ms -- never a launch. The same 15 m from a baro is one.

divergence.note: the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad

scenarios.name: warm_start_into_gliding_rebases_the_backstop
scenarios.note: Regression: a warm start straight into GLIDING never saw BOOSTING; the RSO backstop is based on the first tick, so it still bounds the restored flight -- flight_timeout_ms after that tick, not after boot.

scenarios.name: warm_start_into_boosting_rearms_everything
scenarios.note: Regression: a warm start into BOOSTING bases the arming window, the burnout timeout and the backstop on the first tick; the apogee then deploys from the restored climb.

scenarios.name: barometer_dropout
scenarios.note: Regression: a baro dropout. On the pad it drains the altitude dwell; in BOOSTING the apogee tracker keeps its open dwell through the gap (no reading is not a rise) and deploys on the first fresh sample; in GLIDING with the laser out of range it resets the landing dwell.

divergence.note: the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad
plan B's BOOSTING reaches the port as a move from outside, recorded external; every later step is plan B's

scenarios.name: gnss_elevation_in_flight
scenarios.note: Corner: plan B gates the GNSS elevation out of the LAUNCH detector only. With both baros stale it feeds the apogee tracker and the landing fallback.

scenarios.name: apogee_dwell_is_launch_ms
scenarios.note: Regression: the apogee dwell reuses launch_ms (plan B passes it to apogee_step; ported faithfully). With launch_ms 300 the fall must hold 300 ms.

scenarios.name: a_long_hold_ends_in_two_records
scenarios.note: Corner: BOOSTING detected, then an operator holds GLIDING past the flight timeout. A held stage is not looked at, so `stage auto` shows the move as external AND fires the backstop on the same tick: two sequencer.csv rows from one tick.

scenarios.name: done_until_the_operator
scenarios.note: Corner: DONE has no detector and the backstop does not apply to it; `stage setting` starts a new pad session whose launch dwell starts afresh.

scenarios.name: still_band_edges
scenarios.note: Corner: the still band is 1 +/- still_g (0.3) on |a|, compared squared. 0.69 g and 1.31 g held past ground_ms are not still; one out-of-band sample resets a running dwell (0.71 g from 850 confirms at 1300, not 1150); 0.71 g and 1.29 g, each held ground_ms on its own, confirm (`stage landing` + `stage auto` re-enter LANDING between them); and the band is on the vector: |(0.3, 0.4, 0.95)| is 1.07 g.

scenarios.name: stale_accel_never_settles
scenarios.note: Corner: a dead accel extrapolating a plausible 1 g reads as no reading, so LANDING ends on its timeout, not on a stillness nobody measured; a stale 8 g on the pad is no launch either.

scenarios.name: barometer_landing_below_the_pad
scenarios.note: Corner: the baro fallback lands on a negative elevation (a landing below the pad) and prints its sign.

scenarios.name: shipped_defaults
scenarios.note: Corner: an empty config takes plan B setup() defaults -- boost_timeout_ms 6000 there, though config_default ships 12000 -- and the launch threshold is 2.5 g.

scenarios.name: flight_timeout_from_boosting
scenarios.note: Corner: the RSO backstop bounds BOOSTING too. A launch, then no elevation at all (no apogee) and a burnout fallback set past the backstop: flight_timeout_ms after the tick that first sees BOOSTING, DONE.

scenarios.name: separation_while_held
scenarios.note: Corner: an operator holds BOOSTING (`stage boosting` on the bench) and the separation switch opens. Plan B's driver advances a held BOOSTING to GLIDING and the hold stays, so the stage machine sees nothing -- not even a low laser -- until `stage auto`, which records gliding as external and starts the landing dwell.

scenarios.name: on_the_launch_lines
scenarios.note: Strictness: |a| exactly launch_g (3.0 g, 9.0 squared) held 300 ms is no launch, nor is the baro exactly launch_alt_m (10.0 m) held as long; 3.5 g is one.

scenarios.name: on_the_landing_height
scenarios.note: Strictness: a height exactly land_agl_m (5.0 m) held well past land_ms is no landing, from the baro fallback or from the laser; 4.5 m is one.

scenarios.name: on_the_still_band_edges
scenarios.note: Strictness: with still_g 0.5 the band is (0.25, 2.25) in g^2, open at both ends -- |a| exactly 0.5 g and exactly 1.5 g held past ground_ms are not still; 1.0 g is.

scenarios.name: on_the_drop_line
scenarios.note: Strictness: the apogee needs the smoothed elevation BELOW peak - apogee_drop_m. Seeded at 240 m, the reads 224 and 232 smooth to exactly 235.0 (240 - 5) and 235 holds it there: no apogee however long. 230 smooths to 233.75, below the line, and launch_ms later it deploys.

scenarios.name: a_tolerance_of_a_g_or_more
scenarios.note: Corner: still_g is a tolerance around 1 g, and at 1 g or more the band has no lower edge (plan B clamps it to 0): 0.2 g -- near free fall -- reads as still.

scenarios.name: setting_restarts_the_launch_dwell
scenarios.note: Entry: a launch dwell half-credited on the pad, then `stage gliding` + `stage auto` (seen) and much later `stage setting`. SETTING entry restarts the dwell, so the launch needs launch_ms afresh (5100); a kept dwell would span the 4950 ms gap and fire on the first sample at 5000.

scenarios.name: setting_restarts_the_altitude_dwell
scenarios.note: Entry: the same for the baro launch backup -- 15 m half-credited, a seen GLIDING, then `stage setting`: the altitude dwell starts over and launches at 5100.

divergence.note: the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad

scenarios.name: boosting_restarts_the_apogee_tracker
scenarios.note: Entry: a warm BOOSTING tracks a 240 m peak; back to the pad, then `stage boosting` + `stage auto` at 100 m. BOOSTING entry forgets the old peak, so 100 m seeds a new one and holds (a kept 240 m peak would call apogee at once); the fresh tracker deploys on its own peak.

scenarios.name: warm_landing_rebases_the_backstop
scenarios.note: Entry: a warm start straight into LANDING never saw BOOSTING, so the RSO backstop is based on the first tick -- flight_timeout_ms (500) after it, before the landing timeout (1000) could fire.

scenarios.name: apogee_arming_window_opens_on_time
scenarios.note: Entry: the apogee detector arms exactly apogee_arm_ms (100) after BOOSTING entry. 300 m at 99 ms is ignored, so 200 m from 100 ms seeds the peak and holds (armed a millisecond early it would call apogee from 300 m); the fall to 170 m deploys at 200 m.

scenarios.name: a_hold_hides_the_return_to_setting
scenarios.note: Hazard (plan B, ported as is): a hold observes nothing, so `stage gliding` (a fin check) and then `stage setting` never show the machine a stage change and nothing is recorded. The launch dwell half-credited before the hold survives it, and the first boosting sample after it spans the whole 4950 ms gap: launch on ONE sample. In Rust that detected launch also ends the link's reconnects.

scenarios.name: an_advance_undone_before_the_next_tick
scenarios.note: Corner (plan B, ported as is): the machine lands the glider, and `stage gliding` + `stage auto` put it back before the next tick. The stage equals the last one seen, so the move is not recorded; the advance restarted the landing dwell, so the landing needs land_ms afresh.

scenarios.name: launch_altitude_wins_a_tie
scenarios.note: Reason: an 8 g boost and a 15 m baro complete their dwells on the same tick; the baro backup is checked first and its reason is the one recorded.

divergence.note: the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it; its accel launch completes on the same tick

scenarios.name: a_backwards_clock_completes_a_launch
scenarios.note: Reason: the clock steps back 20 ms onto a sample with no reading, which FEEDS the 80 ms credit to 100: the accel launch prints |a|=0.0g, the baro one alt=0m -- and so does a GNSS elevation, which the launch detector refuses.

divergence.note: the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad
plan B's BOOSTING reaches the port as a move from outside, recorded external; every later step is plan B's
the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad

scenarios.name: a_fast_climb_off_the_pad
scenarios.note: Rate gate: the baro climbs 24 m/s off a 0 m pad, over launch_alt_m from 550 (10.8 m): plan B launches launch_ms later, and so does the port, the whole rise within its 1 s window of the pad held launch_ms.

scenarios.name: a_slow_climb_off_the_pad
scenarios.note: Rate gate: the baro climbs 8 m/s off a 0 m pad, over launch_alt_m from 1400 (10.32 m): plan B launches launch_ms later. It never rises 10 m within 1 s, so the port does not -- weather drift of this shape, only slower, launched TMS-7F unarmed on the bench overnight.

divergence.note: the rate gate: the baro never rose launch_alt_m within 1 s above a level it held for launch_ms before this altitude launch, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad

scenarios.name: the_laser_arrives_mid_barometer_landing_dwell
scenarios.note: Handover: the baro fallback reads 3 m and starts the landing dwell; the laser comes into range low too and decides from then on. The one dwell carries on across the handover, so LANDING comes land_ms after the baro first read low, as in plan B.

scenarios.name: a_drifted_pad_at_rest_then_a_fast_climb
scenarios.note: Physics veto: the pad drifted to 4 m, the accel at rest 1 g; then the baro reads 17 m, a 13 m rise in one step, fast enough for the rate gate. Plan B launches launch_ms later; the port holds the altitude launch while every live accel has read at rest for the rate gate window, and stays on the pad.

divergence.note: the at-rest veto: every live accel has read inside the still band for the rate gate window on every step the altitude launch held its condition, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad
plan B's boosting reaches the port as a move from outside, recorded external; every later step is plan B's

scenarios.name: a_dropout_on_a_pad_at_rest_then_a_fast_climb
scenarios.note: Physics veto: the drifted pad and the accel at rest as above, but the accel reads nothing on the step before the climb. A dropout is no movement: the accel's run at rest goes on through it, so the port holds the altitude launch plan B makes, as on the pad without the dropout.

divergence.note: the at-rest veto: every live accel has read inside the still band for the rate gate window on every step the altitude launch held its condition, so the port does not make it and stays on the pad
plan B's boosting reaches the port as a move from outside, recorded external; every later step is plan B's

scenarios.name: a_sustained_boost_with_the_elevation_falling
scenarios.note: Physics veto: warm into BOOSTING under a sustained 8 g on +x while the baro falls from 200 m to 150 m (a pressure wave in the airframe). Plan B calls apogee launch_ms after the smoothed fall crosses the drop line; the port holds the apogee while every live accel's thrust gate still sees the boost.

divergence.note: the thrust veto: every live accel's thrust gate still sees the boost on every step the apogee held its condition, so the port does not call it and stays in BOOSTING
plan B's gliding reaches the port as a move from outside, recorded external; every later step is plan B's

scenarios.name: flight_shipped_config_separation
scenarios.note: Seeded: the config_default sequencer, a clean 4 g boost, the separation switch at the top, a laser landing, still on the ground.

scenarios.name: flight_noise_100_percent
scenarios.note: Seeded: plan B setup() defaults, a 3.2 g x 1.5 s boost under ~100 % accel noise (the leaky dwell must still launch), 1.5 m baro noise with dropped samples, no separation switch, no laser. The arc tops out about 5.8 s into the flight, after the detector arms (apogee_arm_ms 4000 past BOOSTING, about 5.1 s), so the smoothed peak is tracked through the noisy top and its high samples (a raw running maximum would latch one: the measured early-apogee incident), and a baro dropout falls just past the top.

scenarios.name: flight_dropouts_gnss_rocking
scenarios.note: Seeded: test_sequencer-like thresholds, long baro dropouts covered by the GNSS elevation, a laser landing, then rocking on the ground: never still, so the landing timeout ends it.
